additional_info.subject: ID0399515-DC/Si-D/AT[ASl07a] - Less power than expected CRM:00315002248
additional_info.body:
Hi Nenad, good morning.
I apologise for my delay as yesterday was a crazy day :D
Thank you for pointing me out the photo as I failed to understand it was in the webform.
Here is the explanation for the way it worked:
As you can see, the EV indeed can take up to 425kW.
During charging we see these values:
The EVSE_DESpwr is the available power to be provided from the system so let's say that at most, we can provide 400kW with the current system availability.
But from the EV side it's only requesting 789V at 363A = 286.4 kW. Since we use a current source, the current is always correspondent with the value that is requested and the voltage can oscilate a little bit that's why we see this small difference.
Since I couldn't check the session live it's hard for me to say where the root cause lies, it can indeed be our problem or just the EV requested that value due to battery management.
In any case, right now as we speak, there is a session with this exact same EV at 375kW:
This is the EV ID:
ec9468000a75
What is this EV brand and model? My suggestion would be to either report to me as soon as this reoccurs so that I can connect remotely and check the session live or check with the OEM of the EV.
For me it doesn't make sense that the charger only provided this value before and there was no change, I believe it was a simple request by the EV and there is nothing we can do regarding this.
Please let me know your thoughts and question.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: AW: ID0399515-DC/Si-D/AT[ASl07a] - Less power than expected CRM:00315002248
additional_info.body:
Hi Franciso,
thank you very much for the brief answer.
Actually, we have another interpretation for the power limitation.. maybe you could correct us if we understood this wrong.
The EV is an eActros 600 and can actually charge with 375kW constantly.
Our interpretation is following:
The customer has an OCPP load management on site. Therefore, we checked, if there maybe was a command coming via OCPP to limit the power and found following command:
2025-01-09T11:29:56.723127+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/1909052de0ee[704]: OCPP: Received command: SetChargingProfile (e61f190b-4307-4dda-a3da-2acd8dd60586) - {"connectorId":1,"csChargingProfiles":{"chargingProfileId":1,"stackLevel":1,"chargingProfilePurpose":"TxProfile","chargingProfileKind":"Absolute","chargingSchedule":{"chargingRateUnit":"W","chargingSchedulePeriod":[{"startPeriod":0,"limit":
282000
}],"startSchedule":"0"},"transactionId":108255723}}
As we understood, this is the Smart Charging command, which limits the charger power limit to 282 000W at the beginning of the charging session…. is this right?
But why do the logs show, that EVSE_DESpwr is still 400kW?
BR Nenad
Von:
SI Emobility Technical Support <emobility_support.si@siemens.com>
Gesendet:
Mittwoch, 15. Jänner 2025 10:00
An:

additional_info.subject: ID0399515-DC/Si-D/AT[ASl07a] - Less power than expected CRM:00315002248
additional_info.body:
Hi Nenad,
Thank you for the fast reply. Indeed you are correct this seems to come from the ELMS. I was trying to look for a fault instead, usually from the backend side we can always confirm with them. As I was not aware of how the message from ELMS would come (we don't have access to a ELMS for us to test ourselves in our lab).
In this case the EVSE_DESPwr is just a indication of the available power, so in the case the ELMS would release the limit, the charger would be able to provide 400kW again.
Let me know if you have any more questions :)
Best regards,
Francisco
